newsitem.title: INDIA: Too early to predict EL Nino impact on rains - India.
newsitem.headline: Too early to predict EL Nino impact on rains - India.

text.p: Indian Agriculture Minister Chaturanan Mishra was quoted on Wednesday as saying that it was too early to say if El Nino warm water currents would affect monsoon rains in the country.

The Press Trust of India (PTI) quoted Mishra as saying he had informed Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral and the Finance Ministry about the likely impact of El Nino warm water currents on foodgrains output. The news agency gave no details.

Mishra said India would need four to five billion rupees ($112 million to $140 million) for early precautionary steps, such as well-digging and water diversion techniques, in case El Nino adversely affected the monsoon.
El Nino raises the water temperature off the coast of South America and can disrupt weather patterns worldwide, creating drought conditions in some areas.

The Indian Meteorological Department (IMD) last month forecast a 10th successive normal monsoon in 1997 but also said the El Nino effect, which is one of the 16 parameters on which its monsoon forecast is based, was showing an "unfavourable trend" this year.
IMD officials said on Tuesday that they were not worried about the impact of El Nino on the progress of monsoon rains.
